lines.caption: "My Lord, under Section 420 of the IPC, the accused is clearly guilty of cheating my client."
"Stop, counsel. IPC 420? That no longer applies. Since 1 July 2024, cheating is BNS 318. Say it again with the right section."
That judge is an AI. And it just cut off counsel for citing a law India replaced in 2024.
India has 5.64 crore court cases pending.
More than 80% of Indians qualify for free legal aid. By 2019, only about 1.5 crore had ever used it.
Because when your boss stops paying you, you do not think in sections and forms. You just want someone to tell you what to do next.
And the young lawyer who takes that case? India's criminal laws changed in July 2024. New names, new numbers. And when they rehearse at midnight, nobody pushes back.
So we built न्यायमित्र. A friend in court, whichever side of it you're on.
Door one: सहाय. You just talk, the way you would to a friend.
"My boss hasn't paid my salary for three months."
"Where was the job: a company, a shop, a contractor, or with a person?"
She asks one thing at a time. Then she puts your path on screen: where to go, what to carry, your deadline, and a notice she drafts for you.
The steps come from a checked legal knowledge base, not the model's imagination. And a free lawyer is one call away, on 15100.
Door two: अभ्यास. A full hearing, in five rounds. You argue, opposing counsel hits back, and the bench scores you both.
"My Lord, showing a few UPI payments does not erase the offence under Section 318 BNS."
In this hearing, our test lawyer argued against their own client by mistake. The bench noticed.
"Counsel, by alleging dishonest intention against your own client, you are weakening their case."
Then it writes the verdict, and the one line you should have said.

Under the hood, it runs on Gnani. Prisma listens, even when Hindi and English mix. Timbre speaks, in ten Indian languages. Evon reasons, and if a route goes down, Gemini takes over in seconds, so the conversation never stops.
Every voice in this film is Timbre.
"Justice belongs to everyone."
Justice should speak your language. Try न्यायमित्र. The link is in the post.
